newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Banking sector lifts Moroccan bourse.
newsitem.headline: Banking sector lifts Moroccan bourse.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour session on Monday 0.55 percent higher, lifted by the banking sector notably and, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 495.79 points from 493.06 points on Friday.
"Last week we felt that the prices were rising because of a lack of liquidity, now the values seem to readjust," a broker at Casablanca based Maroc Services Intermediation said.
Consumer credit firm Credor, floated on the bourse in December 1996, which gained 94 dirhams last week, shed three dirhams to close at 690 dirhams.
"Credor was getting too high, we expected the trend to reverse," he added.
In the banking sector, Wafabank, one of the market's liquid stocks, jumped 19 dirhams to close at 682 dirhams.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique, rose five dirhams to close at 183 dirhams. Morocco said it would soon sell its 34.57 percent stake in the bank.

Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the leading banks, was up 13 dirhams to close at 433 dirhams. BMCE plans to cut its interest rate by 0.25 percent on loans to small and medium enterprises starting from February 1.

ONA group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, closed at 625 dirhams, one dirham lower from the previous session. The conglomerate, which holds stakes in more than 100 firms, is the first in terms of market capitalisation with more than 10 billion dirhams.

Second largest holding, Societe nationale d'Investissement, remained unchanged at 564 dirhams. Casablanca Finance Intermediation said in a recent report that SNI's consolidated net result for 1996 was estimated at 340 million dirhams ($36.9 million) 40 million dirhams more than earlier forecasts on expectation of bigger capital gains.
Traded volume on the official market was 35.3 from 81.1 million dirhams last Friday.
